sections.html:
Bacon County is a rural, low-density county in southeast Georgia, and Alma is its seat. About 11,070 people live here, a hair below the 11,140 counted in 2020, which works out to roughly 39 people per square mile. A typical listing is a house on a country lot, often with a well, a septic tank and room for outbuildings.

Alma is the only city. Rockingham is a census-designated place, and Coffee and Sessoms are unincorporated, so many sellers hold land outside any city limits.

sections.h2: Home values and what buyers compare
sections.html:
This is one of the least expensive housing markets in Georgia, and 68.6% of housing units are owner-occupied.

Bacon County housing figures, 2020-2024 unless noted

Housing units (July 2025)4,863

Residents in the same house a year earlier93.3%

Fourteen permits in all of 2025 means almost no new houses are going up, so a shopper compares your property with older stock. With 93.3% of residents staying put for a year, turnover is slow. Price against nearby recent closings rather than a statewide figure.

In 2020 about 11.6% of the county's 4,807 housing units stood vacant, and 31.7% of occupied units were rented. Those vacant houses are one reason your listing may sit beside several others that need work.

sections.h2: Which office handles what in Alma
sections.html:
The tax commissioner and the assessors work from the Bacon County Government Building, 502 West 12th Street, Suite 101, Alma, GA 31510. The tax commissioner's website posts one phone line, 912-632-5614, and office hours of 9:00 am to 5:00 pm.

  • Suite 101, tax commissioner: bills, payments, liens and mobile home permits
  • Suite 101, tax assessors: values, returns, exemptions and appeals
  • Suite 200, Clerk of Superior Court: copies of deeds

Parcel lookups run through qPublic. Treat the website as general information. The Official Code of Georgia controls if anything differs, so call the office when the amount matters.

Bills are normally due November 15 and are mailed at least two months earlier. The county warns that the date can change, so go by the one printed on your own bill.

Two installments are allowed, though the unpaid portion keeps collecting charges after the deadline. A mailed payment counts if the postmark is on or before the due date, and a due date on a weekend or holiday rolls to the next business day. You can also drive up to the drop box on the right side of the front parking lot. Card payments add a 2.75% charge from the processor, with a $2.00 floor.

  • Monthly interest runs at prime plus three percentage points
  • Penalty of 5% of the tax lands 120 days after the due date, repeats every 120 days, and stops at 20%
  • A homesteaded parcel with a bill under $500 owes no penalty
  • Mobile homes follow a separate April 1 deadline and a 10% penalty

sections.h2: Can a tax lien follow a Bacon County sale?
sections.html:
Yes, if the bill stays open. Once a bill is 30 days late the office can file a FiFa, which is a lien recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court on the General Execution Docket. The county warns that the entry can stay on a credit file for seven years or longer. Delinquent notices go out only at intervals, so call for the current amount before you pay.

Under Georgia law the lien lands on whoever owned the property on January 1. To move it to the buyer, bring the signed closing statement to Suite 101 within 90 days after the due date. A bill that reaches you after you sold belongs in the buyer's hands.

  1. Ask Suite 101 for a written payoff figure.
  2. Have the title company pay it from your sale proceeds.
  3. Keep a copy of your settlement statement.

You have 45 days, counted from the date printed on the assessment notice. Send the assessors a written dispute on the uniform state form, and name your ground: taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption.

Your filing also picks the route the case takes. On the Board of Equalization track, the assessors may first revise the figure, which gives you 30 days to answer an amended notice. Whatever stays unresolved goes before the board, and Superior Court is the next step after that. A hearing officer track exists for non-homestead real estate above a value threshold. Arbitration requires a certified appraisal and ends the matter.

Separately, the January 1 to April 1 return period lets you declare your own value. Real estate returns renew themselves each year, while personal property returns need filing annually.

sections.h2: Exemptions that can lower the bill
sections.html:
Homestead is the big one for owner-occupants. A statewide baseline applies, Bacon County layers its own exemptions on top, and the bigger of the two is what you get. You must have owned and lived in the house on January 1, and the form must reach the assessors by April 1 of your first claim year. After approval it renews itself.

  • Deferral for homeowners 62 and up whose household income is no more than $15,000
  • Qualifying farmland: assessed at 30% rather than 40%
  • Conservation Use and Forest Land Protection: valued by current use, with a 10 or 15 year covenant
  • Historic and brownfield programs: filed in the same January to April window

Call 912-632-5614 for the local amounts and what proof to bring. Claiming homestead on a second property anywhere, in or out of Georgia, is unlawful.

Begin with the number. Find out what is owed for each open year, whether a FiFa exists, and, if the house is a mobile home, whether the April 1 permit tax is paid. Then choose between paying before you list and paying at the closing table.

Inherited houses, rentals and vacant properties often carry several unpaid years, and a title search will surface every recorded lien. If your land sits in a conservation or forest program, ask the assessors what the covenant demands of a new owner before you list, since a buyer will ask.

When you visit Suite 101, bring your deed or parcel number, your latest bill and, if you are already under contract, the signed closing statement. A cash buyer who purchases as-is can close without waiting on repairs, but the tax balance still gets settled from your proceeds at the table. A sale that skips listing, showings and buyer financing also skips the weeks of waiting on a lender appraisal, which matters when a bill or lien deadline is close.

If you sell after the bill is mailed but before it is due, settle who pays it in the contract. Put the payoff in writing, keep the receipt, and send the office a copy of the closing statement so the record follows the new owner.

faqs.q: What share of market value is taxed in Bacon County?
faqs.a: Forty percent of fair market value is the assessed value, and exemptions come off that figure before the millage rate is applied. The county commissioners and the school board set the rate each year.

faqs.q: How can I pay a Bacon County bill?
faqs.a: Pay at Suite 101 of the Government Building in Alma, by mail with a postmark on or before the deadline, in the drop box, or online with a card. Questions go to 912-632-5614.

faqs.q: Does selling split the bill between buyer and seller?
faqs.a: Your closing statement does that, not the county. Bring the signed statement to Suite 101 within 90 days after the due date if you want a lien recorded against the buyer.

faqs.q: Is there a refund if I sell in March?
faqs.a: No. Georgia law makes the owner on January 1 responsible for the entire year, and it allows no refund for a part-year owner.

faqs.q: Who sends the notice of my home's value?
faqs.a: The Board of Tax Assessors in the same building. Call 912-632-5614, and watch the 45-day clock that starts on the date printed on the notice.
